learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the principles of theory of machines and mechanisms.
Knowledge and skills for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Develop commitment to the society in which we live so that it prospers through the dimensions of democratic values and sustainability, materialized within the global framework that defines it at all times.
Collaborate actively with a group of people to achieve a common goal, combining different talents.
Reason reflectively about a topic, being able to deliberate on its validity by subjecting one's own and external convictions to debate.
Understand and regulate one's own emotions and those of others to interact and participate effectively and constructively in social and professional life.
Design and perform a new task or project differently using creativity and curiosity to add value with an entrepreneurial attitude.

Use continuous learning and develop autonomous and flexible learning strategies throughout life to be part of an active, motivated, and integrated citizenry, fostering job improvement or personal development.
Kinematically analyze a mechanical system, both planar and 3D, calculating velocities and accelerations of any of its points.
Apply the concepts of motion composition to the analysis of complex movements.
Know the concept of instantaneous center of rotation and its application in planar systems for determining velocities.
Define and identify the parameters of motion of a mechanical system and its degrees of freedom.

Perform dynamic, and where appropriate static, analysis of a mechanical system, using the free body diagram as the main tool. Identify and calculate the forces generated in the interaction between the integral elements of a mechanical system.
Determine and apply the concepts of center of mass and inertia tensor to the integral elements of a mechanical system.
Apply vectorial theorems and the energy theorem to mechanical systems and interpret the obtained results.
Understand the phenomenon of friction, in both static and dynamic situations.
Develop simulations of the behavior of mechanical systems using computer programs.

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 15% from practices and 85% from a final exam. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required on the final exam. The score for the statics problem (15% of the final exam's value) will be the higher of the score obtained in the partial statics test and the score obtained for the statics problem in the final exam. The evaluation system is the same for continuous and global assessment.
